documents.t: Соединением владеет одна задача, runner; дескрипторы обращаются к ней через память брокера, а устройство читает пакет в буфер, который заимствует доставка.
Части ruststream-rust-mqtt, которыми пользуется сервис на MQTT, по странице на каждую.
MqttBroker connects a service to an MQTT 5 server over the memory the board declares; its runner owns the connection, and a device spawns it as a task.
MqttConfig holds where the broker connects and as whom: the address, the client id, the keep-alive, the credentials and the session.
MqttState is the memory of a device broker: three numbers fix how many deliveries are held at once, the largest packet and how many subscriptions are open.
Network is the link the runner connects over: embassy-net on a device, compio's TCP stream on a host, or a link of the board's own.
MqttPublish is the publish policy of a mount: the quality of service and the retain flag of every message it publishes.
Headers travel as MQTT 5 user properties; content-type, reply-to and correlation-id take the matching properties.
A retained message is kept by the server, which hands the last one of each topic to every new subscription that is not shared.
The steps qos and retain on the publish builder reopen, for one message, what the policy of the mount fixed.
An ack sends PUBACK at QoS 1 and PUBREC at QoS 2; QoS 0 has no acknowledgement.
MQTT has no negative acknowledgement: retry answers Unsupported and leaves the delivery unacknowledged.
retry_after publishes a copy of the delivery after a delay: to its own topic for MqttTopic, to a topic the mount site names for MqttFilter.
MqttTopic subscribes to one topic a publisher can name, and answers for its own retry copies.
Two handlers on one filter are one subscription on the server, so they take the messages in turn.
MqttFilter subscribes to every topic its wildcards match: + matches one level and # matches the rest.
Qos picks at most once, at least once or exactly once; a delivery arrives at the lower of the publisher's and the subscription's level.
A shared subscription hands each message to one member of a group, so boards that run the same service share the work.
The embedded TestApp runs a device service on the host with the broker connected in process, and the test drives it with publish, advance and assertions.
The compio TestApp runs a service on the test's own compio runtime, with the broker connected in process.
A live test runs the service against a real server; the stand is mosquitto, started by just test-brokers.
На хосте compio брокер это вариант с кучей, а MqttBroker::compio запускает runner на ядре, которое его подключает, так что сервис - обработчик и приложение.
У сервиса для устройства нет кучи: обработчик заимствует полезную нагрузку из буфера приёма, память брокера это static, а main запускает runner и приложение.
Сервис для устройства тестируют на хосте через embedded TestApp, сервис на compio через compio TestApp; оба подключают брокер внутри процесса.

Крейт ruststream-rust-mqtt реализует брокер MQTT 5 для RustStream для рантаймов embassy и compio. У крейта два варианта. Вариант для устройства обходится без кучи: плата объявляет память брокера как static, а доставка заимствует полезную нагрузку из её буфера приёма. Вариант с кучей (фича alloc, которую включает compio) работает поверх клиента rust-mqtt и подходит хосту compio или устройству, у которого есть куча. Начните с варианта, под который вы собираете сервис: первый сервис на устройстве или первый сервис на хосте compio. Тестирование сервиса для устройства показывает, как запустить любой из них на хосте до того, как он попадёт на плату.

Этот раздел показывает, где ruststream-rust-mqtt находится между брокером MQTT и рантаймом RustStream. Runner и ручки объясняет, как соединением владеет одна задача, а обработчики, издатели и подтверждения обращаются к ней. Во что обходятся доставка и публикация называет, что каждая из них берёт у устройства.

Пакет PUBLISH читается из сокета в буфер приёма памяти брокера, ровно на столько байт, сколько указывает фиксированный заголовок. Доставка держит этот буфер и заимствует из него тему и полезную нагрузку, поэтому между сокетом и обработчиком полезная нагрузка не копируется. Заголовки пакета разбираются в доставку, а буфер возвращается брокеру, когда обработчик завершает доставку или уничтожает её. Пакет, который попадает в несколько подписок, копируется один раз в буфер приёма каждой подписки, кроме первой. Публикация кодируется в один из двух буферов отправки, и runner его записывает. Издатель одалживает байты, а Ok означает, что пакет протокола ушёл в сессию. Подтверждение это команда в очереди фиксированного размера, а пакет протокола отправляет runner. Ничего не выделяется ни при запуске, ни на сообщение: каждый буфер входит в MqttState, который объявляет плата, а его размер равен (MESSAGES + 2) * PACKET байт плюс небольшая часть на каждую подписку.

Клиент rust-mqtt 0.6 отводит каждому принятому полю свой буфер в куче, поэтому доставка берёт по буферу на поле: тему, полезную нагрузку и каждое строковое свойство. Буферы переходят в сообщение без копирования и освобождаются, когда сообщение уничтожается. Публикация копирует байты сообщения в слот записи. Буферы слота сохраняют ёмкость, поэтому публикация ничего не выделяет, как только слоты вместили самое большое сообщение сервиса. Издатель одалживает байты, а Ok означает, что пакет протокола ушёл в сессию. Подтверждение это команда в очереди фиксированного размера. Оно ничего не выделяет, а пакет протокола отправляет runner. Все очереди фиксируются при запуске: 32 команды, 8 слотов записи и 16 доставок на каждую подписку. На compio сеть добавляет одно копирование на каждое чтение: io_uring читает в буфер, которым владеет сам, а клиент читает из него.

Бенчмарки стоимости кода в репозитории считают, во что обходится одно сообщение сервису на ядре, которое его выполняет: инструкции под callgrind и выделения под DHAT, релизные сборки с fat LTO, разность между прогоном на 500 и на 1000 сообщений против mosquitto. Для измерения вариант для устройства работает на хосте, его приложение и runner выполняются в одном потоке. Во что обходится одно сообщение Вариант для устройства Вариант с кучей на compio ruststream-rumqttc Доставка с QoS 1 и подтверждением 6 866 инструкций, 0 выделений 10 210 инструкций, 2,18 выделения 8 937 инструкций, 1,15 выделения Публикация (стоимость ответа за вычетом доставки) 4 297 инструкций, 0 выделений 12 085 инструкций, 0,29 выделения 8 832 инструкции, 6,06 выделения Сервис для устройства читает и отправляет сырые байты, а два других декодируют и кодируют тело JSON, поэтому в его инструкциях нет кодека. just bench-code измеряет вариант с кучей, а just bench-code-noalloc вариант для устройства.

Соединением с сервером владеет одна задача, runner. Ручки сервиса (подписки, издатели и подтверждения обработчиков) обращаются к ней через хранилище, которое существует с самого начала: на устройстве это MqttState платы, в варианте с кучей это очереди, которые брокер создаёт при сборке.

Runner единственный касается сокета. Он обслуживает один цикл: пакеты протокола от сервера, команды от ручек и таймер keep-alive. Каждый из трёх шагов завершается, не дожидаясь остальных, поэтому подтверждение обработчика никогда не стоит в очереди за чтением. Runner берёт из пула буфер приёма, читает в него один пакет, ровно на столько байт, сколько указывает фиксированный заголовок, и разбирает его как представление над этими байтами. Пакет PUBLISH уходит в подходящую подписку, а доставка держит буфер: её тема и полезная нагрузка это срезы буфера. Буфер возвращается в пул, когда обработчик завершает доставку. Когда заняты все буферы приёма, runner перестаёт читать соединение, пока обработчик не завершит одну из доставок. Это и есть управление потоком на устройстве, а число буферов равно MESSAGES памяти брокера. Издатель кодирует публикацию в один из двух буферов отправки, и runner её записывает. Буфер возвращается в пул, когда runner записал пакет протокола, а если заняты оба, издатель ждёт свободного. Runner назначает идентификаторы пакетов для QoS 1 и 2, придерживает публикацию, пока достигнут максимум приёма сервера, и завершает рукопожатия QoS 2. Когда соединение заканчивается, по завершению работы или из-за потери, runner отвечает на каждую ожидающую команду, сообщает каждой ручке, что брокер закрыт, и ждёт следующего подключения. Ручка, использованная после этого, отвечает ошибкой и никогда не сообщает об успехе, которого соединение не совершало.

Runner единственный касается клиента. Он обслуживает один цикл: пакеты протокола от сервера, команды от ручек и таймер keep-alive. Каждый из трёх шагов завершается, не дожидаясь остальных, поэтому подтверждение обработчика никогда не стоит в очереди за чтением. У подписки есть очередь из 16 доставок. Когда очередь полна, runner перестаёт читать соединение, пока обработчик не возьмёт одну. Это и есть управление потоком в этом крейте. Публикация копирует свои байты в один из 8 слотов и отправляет runner команду. Слот возвращается в пул, когда runner записал пакет протокола. Команды ждут в очереди из 32, а отправитель, если она полна, ждёт места. Когда соединение заканчивается, по завершению работы или из-за потери, runner отвечает на каждую ожидающую команду, сообщает каждой ручке, что брокер закрыт, и ждёт следующего подключения. Ручка, использованная после этого, отвечает ошибкой и никогда не сообщает об успехе, которого соединение не совершало. На устройстве runner работает задачей рядом с задачей приложения. На хосте compio брокер запускает его на ядре, которое подключает брокер.
Части ruststream-rust-mqtt, которыми пользуется сервис на MQTT, по странице на каждую.

MqttBroker connects a service to an MQTT 5 server, and the MqttRunner that comes with it owns the connection. On a device, MqttBroker::new takes the MqttState the board declared as a static and a MqttConfig, and returns the broker with its runner. The state is taken for the life of the program, so one state serves one broker. Building the broker performs no I/O, so the whole service fits the synchronous app builder. The runner performs every read and write on the connection, and the handles of the service (subscriptions, publishers, acknowledgements) talk to it. It waits until the app connects the broker, opens the connection over a network, serves it until the app shuts the broker down or the connection is lost, and then waits for the next connect. A device spawns the runner as a task of its own, next to the task of the app. The app starts only while the runner runs, because connecting the broker waits for the runner to open the connection. The broker moves through three types. connect consumes the broker and returns a ConnectedMqttBroker, and shutdown consumes that and returns a ClosedMqttBroker. A publisher the service kept across the shutdown answers MqttError::NotConnected.

The crate has two variants, chosen by its alloc feature, and each fits one kind of build. The device variant is the default and needs no heap. The crate speaks the protocol itself: a PUBLISH is read into a receive buffer of the state, and the delivery borrows its topic and payload from that buffer. Its settings and descriptors hold &'static str, so they are constants of the firmware. A handler reads the payload as bytes it borrows, with #[derive(Deserialized)], and a reply leaves as the bytes it returns, with #[derive(Serialized)]. The heap variant is the alloc feature, which compio turns on. The broker runs over the rust-mqtt client, which keeps every field it receives in a heap buffer of its own, and the settings hold owned strings. MqttBroker::new(config) takes no state, and on a compio host MqttBroker::compio starts the runner on the core that connects the broker, so the host spawns nothing. A device that has a heap takes this variant too, with alloc and embassy. The guide for a compio host shows it. The features, all off by default: embassy adds the network of a device, alloc selects the heap variant, compio adds the network of a compio host and MqttBroker::compio (and alloc), and testing adds the in-process transport a TestApp connects.

A device service: the handler and the app, then the memory, the runner's task and the start function the board's main calls once its network stack is up. MqttConfig holds where the broker connects and as whom: the address, the client id, the keep-alive, the credentials and the session. On a device every text is a &'static str, so the settings hold no buffer of their own and the firmware keeps them in a const. The password is the device's own: the firmware reads it when it boots and adds it to the constant. On the heap variant the texts are owned, and the service takes the password the deployment hands it when it starts. Building a config performs no I/O. The address is read when the broker connects, and a value the broker cannot connect to is reported there as MqttError::Connect. It is host:port or mqtt://host[:port], with the port defaulting to 1883, and an IPv6 literal keeps its brackets. Another scheme, a port that is not a number and an address with no host are refused. The client id is the identity of the session on the server. It starts empty, which asks the server to assign one, and a session that outlives a connection needs an id of its own. The keep-alive is the interval, in whole seconds, after which the runner pings an idle connection; it defaults to 60 seconds and zero turns pings off. credentials sets the user name and the password, and the Debug form of the config shows the user and never the password. persistent_session resumes the session the server keeps for the client id instead of starting a clean one, and asks the server to keep it for the given time after the connection ends. The server then redelivers the QoS 1 and QoS 2 messages that a previous connection left unacknowledged.

The server on the plant network, as the valve valve-1, with a session the server keeps for ten minutes. A device keeps the address, the client id, the keep-alive and the session in a const, and adds the password it was provisioned with when it boots. examples/device/device_config.rs /// The server on the plant network, as this valve. These texts are literals of the firmware, so /// the settings are a constant. The server keeps the session for ten minutes after the /// connection ends and redelivers what the valve had not acknowledged. const VALVE: MqttConfig = MqttConfig::new("mqtt://192.168.1.10:1883") .client_id("valve-1") .keep_alive(Duration::from_secs(30)) .persistent_session(Duration::from_secs(600)); /// The settings with the password the plant provisioned into this valve, which the firmware /// reads when it boots: a secret is not a literal of the firmware. const fn provisioned(password: &'static str) -> MqttConfig { VALVE.credentials("valve-1", password) }

MqttState is the memory a broker of the device variant owns: the receive buffers a delivery borrows from, the send buffers a publish is encoded into, the table of subscriptions and the channels between the handles and the runner. It is one value of known size that the board declares as a static, so nothing is allocated, at startup or per message. Three numbers fix its size, and they are the type's parameters: MqttState<MESSAGES, PACKET, SUBSCRIPTIONS> with the defaults 4, 1024 and 8. The broker, its runner and its deliveries carry the same three numbers, and a broker over the defaults is named MqttBroker alone. MESSAGES is the number of receive buffers. A delivery holds one from its arrival until its handler settles it or drops it, so this is how many deliveries wait or are in hand at once. The session asks the server to keep at most one fewer QoS 1 and 2 deliveries in flight, so a buffer stays free for the server's answers. When every buffer is held, the runner stops reading the connection until a handler settles one: that is the back-pressure of the device, and it reaches the server through the TCP window. A device whose handlers are slow, or that acknowledge late, takes more buffers; the minimum is two. PACKET is the size in bytes of each receive buffer and each send buffer, so it is the largest packet in either direction. The session announces it to the server as its maximum packet size, and the server never sends a larger one. A publish that does not fit is refused before it is sent, and the message is handed back to the caller. The packet holds the fixed header, the topic and the properties besides the payload, so the largest payload is smaller than PACKET. The minimum is 64. SUBSCRIPTIONS is how many subscriptions are open at once, one for each mounted descriptor. The minimum is one. A PUBLISH that reaches several subscriptions is copied into a receive buffer for each one beyond the first, so it holds as many buffers as there are subscriptions it matches. The memory it takes is about (MESSAGES + 2) * PACKET bytes, the two being the send buffers, plus a small part for each subscription and each message. The numbers are checked when the state is built, in a const context, so a value below a minimum does not compile.

Six deliveries of up to 512 bytes and four subscriptions, about 4 KiB of the board's RAM. More frames than buffers pass through it, because a settled buffer returns to the broker. examples/device/device_memory.rs /// Six deliveries of up to 512 bytes, and four subscriptions: about 4 KiB of the board's RAM. type Memory = MqttState<6, 512, 4>; static MQTT: ConstStaticCell<Memory> = ConstStaticCell::new(MqttState::new()); /// The broker over that memory, named by the same three numbers. type Mqtt = MqttBroker<6, 512, 4>;

Network is the link the runner connects over: it opens a stream to a host and a port, and it sleeps on the clock of the runtime the runner runs on. The stream is anything that reads and writes through embedded-io-async, and a read of it must be cancel-safe: the runner stops waiting for the next packet of the server when a handle sends it work, and picks the read up again afterwards. A device uses EmbassyNetwork (feature embassy): a TCP socket on an embassy-net stack, over a receive buffer and a send buffer that the task of the runner owns. The runner reads a packet from the socket straight into a receive buffer of the broker's memory, exactly as long as the fixed header of the packet says, so a PUBLISH stays where it arrived and the delivery borrows from it. A host name in the address is resolved by the DNS client of the stack, and an IPv4 literal is used as it is. A failure is an EmbassyConnectError: the name did not resolve, or the TCP connection failed. A compio host, on the heap variant, uses CompioNetwork (feature compio), and MqttBroker::compio starts the runner over it. io_uring reads into a buffer it owns until the read completes, so a task of the connection reads the stream into owned buffers and the client reads out of them. That costs one copy per read, and a read the client stops waiting for loses nothing. A board with another link, such as a TLS session or the socket of a modem, implements Network for that link; the rustdoc of the trait shows a board's network. Whatever the network, the runner takes it as an argument of MqttRunner::run.

MqttPublish is the publish policy of a mount: the quality of service and the retain flag of every message it publishes. A policy is a plain declaration that holds no connection, and the runtime pairs it with the connected broker into an MqttPublisher. qos defaults to Qos::AtLeastOnce and retain to false. The policy is also the default of the broker, so a reply and a retry copy leave through it unless the mount names another. On a device the publisher encodes the message straight into a send buffer of the broker's memory, which the runner writes, and a message that does not fit the packet is refused with the message handed back. On the heap variant the publisher copies the bytes of a message into a staging slot of the broker, whose buffers keep their capacity, so a publish allocates nothing once the slots have held the largest message the service sends. Ok means the PUBLISH packet went out into the session; at QoS 1 and 2 the session keeps the message until the server acknowledges it. A publish to a topic no server takes, such as one with a wildcard, is refused with MqttError::Publish, and a publish after the shutdown answers MqttError::NotConnected. A refused publish hands its message back.

A device reports every reading in degrees, and the reports are sent exactly once. Headers travel as MQTT 5 user properties, and content-type, reply-to and correlation-id take the matching properties of the protocol. A serde struct is the contract of a message's headers, and each field is one property whose value is a string. The handler reads them with the Headers extractor, and a publish writes them with with_headers. A textual content type also sets the payload format indicator, and correlation-id is binary on the wire. A header whose name or value is not UTF-8 text without control characters is refused with MqttError::Publish, except the correlation id. The header partition-key (PARTITION_KEY_HEADER) is the key that keyed workers order a subscription's deliveries by.

The state leaves with the trace id the command arrived with. Macros Manual examples/mqtt_publishing_headers.rs /// The state goes out with the trace the command arrived with. #[subscriber(MqttTopic::new("valves/v1/set"))] async fn set( command: &Command, Headers(trace): Headers<Trace>, Out(states): Out<impl Publisher<Options = MqttPublishOptions>, States>, ) -> HandlerOutcome { let state = State { open: command.open }; if states .message(&state) .with_headers(&trace) .publish() .await .is_err() { return HandlerOutcome::retry(); } HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app(runtime = embassy)] fn app(broker: MqttBroker) -> EmbeddedApp<impl Mounts> { EmbeddedApp::new().with_broker(broker, |b| { b.include(set).out(States, MqttPublish::default()) }) } examples/manual/mqtt_publishing_headers.rs /// The state goes out with the trace the command arrived with. struct Set; impl<Entry> Handle<Command, (), Outs<(Entry,)>> for Set where Entry: OutEntry<States, Wire: Publisher<Options = MqttPublishOptions>>, { async fn handle( &self, command: &Command, outs: &Outs<(Entry,)>, ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> Result<(), HandlerOutcome> { let Headers(trace) = Headers::<Trace>::from_context(ctx).await?; let state = State { open: command.open }; outs.get(States) .message(&state) .with_headers(&trace) .publish() .await .map_err(|_| HandlerOutcome::retry()) } } fn app(broker: MqttBroker) -> EmbeddedApp<impl Mounts> { EmbeddedApp::new().with_broker(broker, |b| { b.include( subscriber("valves/v1/set", Set) .map_source(|_| MqttTopic::new("valves/v1/set")) .build(), ) .out(States, MqttPublish::default()) }) }

A retained message is kept by the server, which hands the last one of each topic to every new subscription that is not shared. retain(true) on the policy retains every message of the mount, and the step retains one. A dashboard that starts later reads the state without waiting for the next change. Publishing an empty retained payload clears the topic. The subscription receives the retained message at the lower of the two levels, as any other delivery.

The state of the valve is retained, so a subscriber that joins later reads the latest one. An ack sends PUBACK at QoS 1 and PUBREC at QoS 2; QoS 0 has no acknowledgement. A message settles when the handler returns, and the quality of service of the delivery decides what that sends. At QoS 1 and 2 the server keeps a delivery until it is acknowledged, and the client finishes the QoS 2 handshake on its own once the server releases the message. A QoS 0 delivery has no acknowledgement packet, so settling it answers AckError::Unsupported, which the runtime logs as a warning. drop acknowledges the delivery too, because an acknowledgement is the only final answer MQTT has, and the server never sends the message again. retry asks for a negative acknowledgement, which MQTT does not have, and retry_after is the outcome that tries again later. The acknowledgement goes to the runner, which sends it; a delivery settled after the broker shut down answers AckError::Broker, carrying MqttError::NotConnected.

A device agent applies the commands it knows and drops the rest; both answers settle the delivery. MQTT has no negative acknowledgement, so retry answers AckError::Unsupported and leaves the delivery unacknowledged. A nack with requeue set is what retry asks for. The transport has no packet for it, so the delivery stays unacknowledged on the server, which redelivers it when a persistent session resumes. The runtime logs the unsupported answer as a warning and does not send the message again by itself. A handler that wants the delivery back within the session answers retry_after. A nack without requeue is a drop, and it acknowledges.

A job that is not ready to run is answered with retry, and the runtime sees one call. retry_after publishes a copy of the delivery after a delay: to its own topic for MqttTopic, to a topic the mount site names for MqttFilter. The server moves nothing on a negative answer, so the copy is a publish made by the service. A subscription on a topic is reached again by publishing to that topic, and the descriptor reports it, so the mount site names nothing. A subscription on a filter reads many topics and reports no address. There the mount names the destination with .out_retry(policy).to(name), and a chain that names none does not compile. The copy comes back to the subscription when the named topic matches the filter. The copy leaves through the policy of out_retry, such as MqttPublish, and carries the retry count in the RETRY_COUNT_HEADER header. On a device the copy waits in the store of the mount, and .retry_capacity::<N>() after the mount sets how many wait at once.

MqttTopic subscribes to one topic a publisher can name, and answers for its own retry copies. A topic carries no wildcard, so it is a name a publisher can use. A subscription on a topic is reached again by publishing to that topic, which is why the descriptor can say where the copy of a retried delivery goes. A value with a + or a # is refused when the app starts, and the message names MqttFilter as the descriptor that takes it. The topic must not be empty and must be text an MQTT string carries: no control character and no Unicode non-character. qos sets the quality of service the subscription asks for, and shared makes it a shared subscription. A definition written #[subscriber(MqttTopic)] takes its topic from the name given at the mount site.

Two handlers on one filter are one subscription on the server, so they take the messages in turn. A server holds one subscription per filter, and subscribing the same filter again replaces it. So the subscriptions an app opens on one filter are members of one route: they share its deliveries, and each message reaches one of them, the next in order. The members of a share group work the same way. A handler that must see every message reads a filter of its own.

Two handlers on jobs/+: the first takes the first message, the second takes the next, and so on. Macros Manual examples/mqtt_subscriptions_twice.rs /// The first of two handlers on the same filter. #[subscriber(MqttFilter::new("jobs/+"))] async fn first(job: &Job) -> HandlerOutcome { let _ = job.id; HandlerOutcome::ack() } /// The second takes every other message the filter matches. #[subscriber(MqttFilter::new("jobs/+"))] async fn second(job: &Job) -> HandlerOutcome { let _ = job.id; HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app(runtime = embassy)] fn app(broker: MqttBroker) -> EmbeddedApp<impl Mounts> { EmbeddedApp::new().with_broker(broker, |b| b.include(first).include(second)) } examples/manual/mqtt_subscriptions_twice.rs /// The first of two handlers on the same filter. struct First; impl Handle<Job> for First { fn handle( &self, _job: &Job, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { ready(Ok(())) } } /// The second takes every other message the filter matches. struct Second; impl Handle<Job> for Second { fn handle( &self, _job: &Job, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { ready(Ok(())) } } fn app(broker: MqttBroker) -> EmbeddedApp<impl Mounts> { EmbeddedApp::new().with_broker(broker, |b| { b.include( subscriber("jobs/+", First) .map_source(|_| MqttFilter::new("jobs/+")) .build(), ) .include( subscriber("jobs/+", Second) .map_source(|_| MqttFilter::new("jobs/+")) .build(), ) }) }

MqttFilter subscribes to every topic its wildcards match: + matches one level and # matches the rest. One filter reads many topics, so it addresses none of them. A retry copy cannot go to a filter, and the mount site names where it goes. The delivery keeps the topic it was published to, and MqttMessage::topic returns it. A filter that is not a valid topic filter is refused when the app starts. qos and shared work as on MqttTopic. A definition written #[subscriber(MqttFilter)] takes its filter from the name given at the mount site.

Every sensor of the first floor reports on a topic of its own. Macros Manual examples/mqtt_subscriptions_filter.rs /// Every sensor of the first floor reports on a topic of its own. #[subscriber(MqttFilter::new("floor-1/+/temp"))] async fn log(reading: &Reading) -> HandlerOutcome { let _ = reading.celsius; HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app(runtime = embassy)] fn app(broker: MqttBroker) -> EmbeddedApp<impl Mounts> { EmbeddedApp::new().with_broker(broker, |b| b.include(log)) } examples/manual/mqtt_subscriptions_filter.rs /// Every sensor of the first floor reports on a topic of its own. struct Log; impl Handle<Reading> for Log { fn handle( &self, _reading: &Reading, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { ready(Ok(())) } } fn app(broker: MqttBroker) -> EmbeddedApp<impl Mounts> { EmbeddedApp::new().with_broker(broker, |b| { b.include( subscriber("floor-1/+/temp", Log) .map_source(|_| MqttFilter::new("floor-1/+/temp")) .build(), ) }) }

Qos picks at most once, at least once or exactly once; a delivery arrives at the lower of the publisher's and the subscription's level. A subscription names its level with qos(..) on MqttTopic or MqttFilter, and the default is Qos::AtLeastOnce. Level QoS What the protocol does AtMostOnce 0 sends the message once, with no acknowledgement; a message lost on the way is gone AtLeastOnce 1 resends until the receiver answers PUBACK; a message may arrive twice ExactlyOnce 2 a four-packet handshake, so the message arrives once The server sends each message at the lower of two levels: the one its publisher sent it at and the one the subscription asked for. So a QoS 2 subscription receives a QoS 0 publish at QoS 0, and MqttMessage::qos tells the level a delivery arrived at. A delivery at QoS 1 or 2 is acknowledged when the handler settles it. The level a publish is sent at is a setting of the publish policy.

Telemetry read at most once, because the next reading replaces a lost one, and a valve command read exactly once. Macros Manual examples/mqtt_subscriptions_qos.rs /// Telemetry is read at most once: the next reading replaces a lost one. #[subscriber(MqttTopic::new("sensors/temp").qos(Qos::AtMostOnce))] async fn store(reading: &Reading) -> HandlerOutcome { let _ = reading.celsius; HandlerOutcome::ack() } /// A valve command is applied exactly once. #[subscriber(MqttTopic::new("valves/v1/set").qos(Qos::ExactlyOnce))] async fn set(command: &Command) -> HandlerOutcome { let _ = command.open; HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app(runtime = embassy)] fn app(broker: MqttBroker) -> EmbeddedApp<impl Mounts> { EmbeddedApp::new().with_broker(broker, |b| b.include(store).include(set)) } examples/manual/mqtt_subscriptions_qos.rs /// Telemetry is read at most once: the next reading replaces a lost one. struct Store; impl Handle<Reading> for Store { fn handle( &self, _reading: &Reading, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { ready(Ok(())) } } /// A valve command is applied exactly once. struct Set; impl Handle<Command> for Set { fn handle( &self, _command: &Command, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { ready(Ok(())) } } fn app(broker: MqttBroker) -> EmbeddedApp<impl Mounts> { EmbeddedApp::new().with_broker(broker, |b| { let temp = MqttTopic::new("sensors/temp").qos(Qos::AtMostOnce); let valve = MqttTopic::new("valves/v1/set").qos(Qos::ExactlyOnce); b.include( subscriber("sensors/temp", Store) .map_source(|_| temp) .build(), ) .include( subscriber("valves/v1/set", Set) .map_source(|_| valve) .build(), ) }) }

A shared subscription hands each message to one member of a group, so boards that run the same service share the work. shared(group) on MqttTopic or MqttFilter subscribes through $share/<group>/<filter>, an MQTT 5 feature. The server gives each matching message to one subscription of the group instead of to every one. The group name must not be empty and must not contain /, + or #; the descriptor refuses it when the app starts. The server sends no retained message to a shared subscription when it joins. A retry copy of a delivery goes to the plain topic: the $share prefix is a name for subscribing, and a publish to it would reach a topic of that literal spelling.

Every board runs this service, and the server gives each job to one of them. Macros Manual examples/mqtt_subscriptions_shared.rs /// Every board runs this service; the server gives each job to one of them. #[subscriber(MqttTopic::new("jobs/render").shared("renderers"))] async fn render(job: &Job) -> HandlerOutcome { let _ = job.id; HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app(runtime = embassy)] fn app(broker: MqttBroker) -> EmbeddedApp<impl Mounts> { EmbeddedApp::new().with_broker(broker, |b| b.include(render)) } examples/manual/mqtt_subscriptions_shared.rs /// Every board runs this service; the server gives each job to one of them. struct Render; impl Handle<Job> for Render { fn handle( &self, _job: &Job, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { ready(Ok(())) } } fn app(broker: MqttBroker) -> EmbeddedApp<impl Mounts> { EmbeddedApp::new().with_broker(broker, |b| { b.include( subscriber("jobs/render", Render) .map_source(|_| MqttTopic::new("jobs/render").shared("renderers")) .build(), ) }) }

The embedded TestApp runs a device service on the host with the broker connected in process, and the test drives it with publish, advance and assertions. The test hands the production app its broker, built over a static memory the test declares as the board does, and addresses the broker by its type: tb.broker::<MqttBroker>(). The runner is not needed, because the in-process transport replaces the connection. It is a model of the server: it keeps the subscriptions, the retained message of each topic and the share groups, matches filters with wildcards, and delivers at the lower of the two levels. message(..).publish() is a publish of another client of the server, at QoS 1 and not retained. The clock is the test's: advance moves it, and a retry_after copy comes back once its delay has passed. The deliveries a test holds at once are bounded by the memory of the broker: a handler that has not settled a delivery keeps its receive buffer, as on the device. A persistent session and its redelivery, the receive window and the handshakes behind QoS 1 and 2 belong to the server, and the live stand tests them. The assertions on the options of a publish, such as with_options, read the steps and the retain flag of an Out slot.

A job is answered, and the answer is read from the topic it was published to. Macros Manual examples/device/device_testing.rs #[test] fn a_job_is_answered() { static MEMORY: ConstStaticCell<MqttState> = ConstStaticCell::new(MqttState::new()); block_on(async { let tb = TestApp::start(app(board(MEMORY.take()))) .await .expect("the app starts"); let jobs = tb.broker::<MqttBroker>(); jobs.message(&Sent(b"mix")) .to("jobs/run") .publish() .await .expect("the harness publishes"); jobs.subscriber("jobs/run") .assert_called_once() .with_raw(b"mix") .settled(HandlerOutcome::ack()); jobs.published::<()>("jobs/done") .assert_called_once() .with_raw(b"done"); tb.shutdown().await.expect("the app stops"); }); } examples/manual/device_testing.rs #[test] fn a_job_is_answered() { static MEMORY: ConstStaticCell<MqttState> = ConstStaticCell::new(MqttState::new()); block_on(async { let tb = TestApp::start(app(board(MEMORY.take()))) .await .expect("the app starts"); let jobs = tb.broker::<MqttBroker>(); jobs.message(&Sent(b"mix")) .to("jobs/run") .publish() .await .expect("the harness publishes"); jobs.subscriber("jobs/run") .assert_called_once() .with_raw(b"mix") .settled(HandlerOutcome::ack()); jobs.published::<()>("jobs/done") .assert_called_once() .with_raw(b"done"); tb.shutdown().await.expect("the app stops"); }); }

Macros Manual examples/device/device_testing.rs #[test] fn a_job_is_asked_for_again_when_its_delay_has_passed() { static MEMORY: ConstStaticCell<MqttState> = ConstStaticCell::new(MqttState::new()); block_on(async { let tb = TestApp::start(retrying_app(board(MEMORY.take()))) .await .expect("the app starts"); let jobs = tb.broker::<MqttBroker>(); jobs.message(&Sent(b"mix")) .to("jobs/later") .publish() .await .expect("the harness publishes"); tb.advance(Duration::from_secs(4)) .await .expect("the clock moves"); jobs.subscriber("jobs/later").assert_called_once(); tb.advance(Duration::from_secs(1)) .await .expect("the clock moves"); let calls = jobs.subscriber("jobs/later").assert_called(2); assert_eq!(calls.outcomes().last(), Some(&Outcome::Ack)); tb.shutdown().await.expect("the app stops"); }); } examples/manual/device_testing.rs #[test] fn a_job_is_asked_for_again_when_its_delay_has_passed() { static MEMORY: ConstStaticCell<MqttState> = ConstStaticCell::new(MqttState::new()); block_on(async { let tb = TestApp::start(retrying_app(board(MEMORY.take()))) .await .expect("the app starts"); let jobs = tb.broker::<MqttBroker>(); jobs.message(&Sent(b"mix")) .to("jobs/later") .publish() .await .expect("the harness publishes"); tb.advance(Duration::from_secs(4)) .await .expect("the clock moves"); jobs.subscriber("jobs/later").assert_called_once(); tb.advance(Duration::from_secs(1)) .await .expect("the clock moves"); let calls = jobs.subscriber("jobs/later").assert_called(2); assert_eq!(calls.outcomes().last(), Some(&Outcome::Ack)); tb.shutdown().await.expect("the app stops"); }); }

documents.t: The compio TestApp runs a service on the test's own compio runtime, with the broker connected in process. The test is a plain #[test] that blocks on one future of a compio::runtime::Runtime, and the calls are those of the embedded harness. The harness runs the app as the one core of the test's runtime, and MqttBroker::compio needs no runner of its own there. The clock is the runner's virtual clock, which advance moves.

The same job, answered on compio. Macros Manual examples/mqtt_testing_compio.rs #[test] fn a_job_is_answered_on_compio() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> { Runtime::new()?.block_on(async { let tb = TestApp::start(app()).await?; let jobs = tb.broker::<MqttBroker>(); jobs.message(&Job { id: 7 }) .to("jobs/run") .publish() .await?; jobs.subscriber("jobs/run") .assert_called_once() .with(&Job { id: 7 }) .settled(HandlerOutcome::ack()); jobs.published::<Done>("jobs/done") .assert_called_once() .with(&Done { id: 7 }); tb.shutdown().await?; Ok(()) }) } examples/manual/mqtt_testing_compio.rs #[test] fn a_job_is_answered_on_compio() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> { Runtime::new()?.block_on(async { let tb = TestApp::start(app()).await?; let jobs = tb.broker::<MqttBroker>(); jobs.message(&Job { id: 7 }) .to("jobs/run") .publish() .await?; jobs.subscriber("jobs/run") .assert_called_once() .with(&Job { id: 7 }) .settled(HandlerOutcome::ack()); jobs.published::<Done>("jobs/done") .assert_called_once() .with(&Done { id: 7 }); tb.shutdown().await?; Ok(()) }) }

A live test runs the service against a real server, for what the in-process transport leaves to the server: the connection, a persistent session and its redelivery, the handshakes behind QoS 1 and 2. The stand is a mosquitto container with an anonymous listener and one that needs a password. just test-brokers starts it, runs the live suites with RUSTSTREAM_REQUIRE_LIVE set, and stops it. A live test reads the address of the stand from MQTT_TEST_URL; the variable RUSTSTREAM_REQUIRE_LIVE turns a missing stand into a failure, so a test that skipped itself is noticed. The test below runs the service on compio and talks to it as a second client of the same server.

A job published to the server is answered by the service, and the answer comes back through a subscription of the test. examples/mqtt_testing_live.rs #[test] fn a_job_is_answered_through_the_server() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> { // The stand is `just test-brokers`; a run without one has nothing to test. let Ok(url) = std::env::var("MQTT_TEST_URL") else { return Ok(()); }; Runtime::new()?.block_on(async { let running = app().start().await?; // The test is another client of the same server. let client = MqttBroker::compio(MqttConfig::new(url).client_id("tester")) .connect() .await?; let mut answers = MqttTopic::new("live/done").subscribe(&client).await?; let jobs = MqttPublish::default().pair(&client).await?; jobs.publish(OutgoingMessage::new("live/jobs", br#"{"id":7}"#), None) .await .map_err(PublishMessageError::into_error)?; let mut deliveries = core::pin::pin!(answers.stream()); let answer = deliveries.next().await.ok_or("the subscription ended")??; assert_eq!(answer.payload(), br#"{"id":7}"#); answer.ack().await?; client.shutdown().await?; running.shutdown().await?; Ok(()) }) }

На хосте compio сервис состоит из обработчика и приложения. MqttBroker::compio запускает runner на ядре, которое подключает брокер, поверх TCP-потока compio, так что вручную ничего запускать не нужно.

У хоста есть куча, и вариант крейта с кучей её использует: это фича alloc, которую включает compio. Брокер работает поверх клиента rust-mqtt, настройки хранят строки во владении, а обработчики декодируют полезную нагрузку кодеком фреймворка, например json. Брокеру не нужен MqttState, потому что клиент сам выделяет то, что принимает. Устройство с кучей берёт тот же вариант с фичами alloc и embassy. Оно создаёт брокер через MqttBroker::new(config) и запускает runner задачей, как в первом сервисе на устройстве, а обработчики используют типы serde. Устройство без кучи берёт вариант для устройства.
cargo add ruststream --no-default-features --features compio,macros,json cargo add ruststream-rust-mqtt --features compio

Макросы Вручную examples/mqtt_network_compio.rs /// Takes every reading the sensors publish. #[subscriber(MqttTopic::new("sensors/temp"))] async fn store(reading: &Reading) -> HandlerOutcome { let _ = reading.celsius; HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app(runtime = compio, cores = 1)] fn app() -> impl App { let config = MqttConfig::new("mqtt://localhost:1883").client_id("collector"); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("collector", "0.1.0")) .with_broker(MqttBroker::compio(config), |b| b.include(store)) } examples/manual/mqtt_network_compio.rs /// Takes every reading the sensors publish. struct Store; impl Handle<Reading> for Store { fn handle( &self, _reading: &Reading, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { let config = MqttConfig::new("mqtt://localhost:1883").client_id("collector"); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("collector", "0.1.0")).with_broker( MqttBroker::compio(config), |b| { b.include( subscriber("sensors/temp", Store) .map_source(|_| MqttTopic::new("sensors/temp")) .build(), ) }, ) } #[ruststream::app(runtime = compio, cores = 1)] пишет main бинарника, который понимает команду run. cargo run -- run запускает сервис против сервера из конфигурации. Подписка, подтверждение и публикация работают так же, как на устройстве: различаются только сеть, рантайм и память. Тестирование сервиса на compio показывает тест этого приложения.

Runner это задача платы, а брокер принимает одну только конфигурацию. Макросы Вручную examples/mqtt_device.rs /// The runner owns the connection, and the app starts only while it runs. #[embassy_executor::task] async fn mqtt(runner: MqttRunner, stack: Stack<'static>) -> ! { let mut rx = [0; 1024]; let mut tx = [0; 1024]; runner .run(EmbassyNetwork::new(stack, &mut rx, &mut tx)) .await } /// What the board's `main` does once its network stack is up. fn start(spawner: Spawner, stack: Stack<'static>) { let config = MqttConfig::new("192.168.1.10:1883").client_id("sensor-7"); let (broker, runner) = MqttBroker::new(config); spawner.spawn(mqtt(runner, stack).expect("the pool holds the runner's task")); spawner.spawn(app::task(broker).expect("the pool holds the app's task")); } examples/manual/mqtt_device.rs /// The runner owns the connection, and the app starts only while it runs. #[embassy_executor::task] async fn mqtt(runner: MqttRunner, stack: Stack<'static>) -> ! { let mut rx = [0; 1024]; let mut tx = [0; 1024]; runner .run(EmbassyNetwork::new(stack, &mut rx, &mut tx)) .await } /// The app's control: `stop` asks it to shut down, and `health` reads where it is. static CONTROL: Control = Control::new(); /// Runs the app until the control stops it. #[embassy_executor::task] async fn service(broker: MqttBroker) { let _ = app(broker).run(&CONTROL).await; } /// What the board's `main` does once its network stack is up. fn start(spawner: Spawner, stack: Stack<'static>) { let config = MqttConfig::new("192.168.1.10:1883").client_id("sensor-7"); let (broker, runner) = MqttBroker::new(config); spawner.spawn(mqtt(runner, stack).expect("the pool holds the runner's task")); spawner.spawn(service(broker).expect("the pool holds the app's task")); }

У сервиса для устройства нет кучи. Память брокера это static, которое объявляет плата; доставка заимствует полезную нагрузку из буфера приёма этой памяти, а ответ кодируется в её буфер отправки. В этом руководстве мы соберём плату с клапанами, которая применяет команды из темы valves/v1/set и сообщает достигнутое состояние. Сервис состоит из трёх частей: обработчика с приложением, задачи runner, которая владеет соединением MQTT, и main платы, который запускает обе.

cargo add ruststream --no-default-features --features embassy,macros cargo add ruststream-rust-mqtt --features embassy cargo add embassy-executor embassy-net static_cell Фича embassy крейта брокера добавляет EmbassyNetwork, сеть runner поверх стека embassy-net. Пока фича alloc крейта брокера выключена, он остаётся вариантом для устройства, и фреймворк следует за ним: фича ruststream, которой нужна куча, например json, включает alloc фреймворка, и тогда крейту брокера нужна и собственная фича alloc. Устройство с кучей так же берёт вариант с кучей.

Обработчик принимает Command и возвращает достигнутое State. Command это полезная нагрузка в виде пришедших байтов: она заимствует их из буфера приёма брокера, поэтому чтение команды ничего не копирует. State это уходящие байты, и ответ кодируется прямо в буфер отправки. #[ruststream::app(runtime = embassy)] превращает функцию приложения в задачу embassy, app::task. Макросы Вручную examples/device/device_service.rs /// A command as the controller sends its bytes, borrowed from the broker's receive buffer. #[derive(Deserialized)] struct Command<'a>(&'a [u8]); /// The state the valve reports, as the bytes that leave. #[derive(Outgoing, Serialized)] #[outgoing(name = "valves/v1/state")] struct State(&'static [u8]); /// Moves the valve and reports where it is. #[subscriber(MqttTopic::new("valves/v1/set"), reply)] async fn set(command: &Command<'_>) -> State { match command.0 { b"open" => State(b"opened"), _ => State(b"closed"), } } #[ruststream::app(runtime = embassy)] fn app(broker: MqttBroker) -> EmbeddedApp<impl Mounts> { EmbeddedApp::new().with_broker(broker, |b| b.include(set).out_reply(MqttPublish::default())) } examples/manual/device_service.rs /// A command as the controller sends its bytes, borrowed from the broker's receive buffer. struct Command<'a>(&'a [u8]); // `#[derive(Deserialized)]` by hand: the view borrows the payload, and `&Command<'_>` takes the // lane that reads no codec. impl Deserialized for Command<'_> { type Output<'a> = Command<'a>; type Error = Infallible; fn from_payload(payload: &[u8]) -> Result<Command<'_>, Self::Error> { Ok(Command(payload)) } } impl Input for Command<'_> { type Axis = SoloDeserialized<Command<'static>>; } /// The state the valve reports, as the bytes that leave. struct State(&'static [u8]); // `#[derive(Serialized)]` by hand: the bytes, the wire of a typed publish, the shape of a reply. impl Serialized for State { type Error = Infallible; fn wire_bytes(&self, _buf: &mut EncodeBuf) -> Result<WireBytes<'_>, Infallible> { Ok(WireBytes::Own(self.0)) } } impl MessageWire for State { type Wire = SerializedWire; } impl ReplyShape for State { type Body = Self; type Headers = (); type Wire = SerializedReply; } // `#[derive(Outgoing)]` with no `name`, by hand: the mount names the destination. impl OutgoingDestination for State { type Form = CallerName; } impl MessageHeaders for State { type Contract = NoHeaders; } /// Moves the valve and reports where it is. struct Set; impl<'p> Handle<Command<'p>, State> for Set { fn handle( &self, command: &Command<'p>, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<State, HandlerOutcome>> { ready(Ok(match command.0 { b"open" => State(b"opened"), _ => State(b"closed"), })) } } fn app(broker: MqttBroker) -> EmbeddedApp<impl Mounts> { EmbeddedApp::new().with_broker(broker, |b| { b.include( subscriber("valves/v1/set", Set) .map_source(|_| MqttTopic::new("valves/v1/set")) .reply() .to("valves/v1/state") .build(), ) .out_reply(MqttPublish::default()) }) }

MqttState это вся память, которой владеет брокер: буферы приёма, из которых заимствуют доставки, буферы отправки и таблица, где хранятся подписки. Плата объявляет её как static и один раз передаёт в MqttBroker::new, который возвращает брокер вместе с его runner. Runner владеет соединением: он открывает его, когда приложение подключает брокер, и через него проходят все чтения, записи и подтверждения. Поэтому плата запускает две задачи: runner поверх сетевого стека и приложение с брокером. Буферы сокета живут в задаче runner, а их размер выбирает плата. Макросы Вручную examples/device/device_service.rs /// The broker's memory: four deliveries of up to 1 KiB, and eight subscriptions. static MQTT: ConstStaticCell<MqttState> = ConstStaticCell::new(MqttState::new()); /// The runner owns the connection, and the app starts only while it runs. #[embassy_executor::task] async fn mqtt(runner: MqttRunner, stack: Stack<'static>) -> ! { let mut rx = [0; 1024]; let mut tx = [0; 1024]; runner .run(EmbassyNetwork::new(stack, &mut rx, &mut tx)) .await } /// What the board's `main` does once its network stack is up. fn start(spawner: Spawner, stack: Stack<'static>) { let config = MqttConfig::new("192.168.1.10:1883").client_id("valve-1"); let (broker, runner) = MqttBroker::new(MQTT.take(), config); spawner.spawn(mqtt(runner, stack).expect("the pool holds the runner's task")); spawner.spawn(app::task(broker).expect("the pool holds the app's task")); } examples/manual/device_service.rs /// The broker's memory: four deliveries of up to 1 KiB, and eight subscriptions. static MQTT: ConstStaticCell<MqttState> = ConstStaticCell::new(MqttState::new()); /// The runner owns the connection, and the app starts only while it runs. #[embassy_executor::task] async fn mqtt(runner: MqttRunner, stack: Stack<'static>) -> ! { let mut rx = [0; 1024]; let mut tx = [0; 1024]; runner .run(EmbassyNetwork::new(stack, &mut rx, &mut tx)) .await } /// The app's control: `stop` asks it to shut down, and `health` reads where it is. static CONTROL: Control = Control::new(); /// Runs the app until the control stops it. #[embassy_executor::task] async fn service(broker: MqttBroker) { let _ = app(broker).run(&CONTROL).await; } /// What the board's `main` does once its network stack is up. fn start(spawner: Spawner, stack: Stack<'static>) { let config = MqttConfig::new("192.168.1.10:1883").client_id("valve-1"); let (broker, runner) = MqttBroker::new(MQTT.take(), config); spawner.spawn(mqtt(runner, stack).expect("the pool holds the runner's task")); spawner.spawn(service(broker).expect("the pool holds the app's task")); } По умолчанию MqttState рассчитан на четыре доставки до 1 КиБ; подписки в нём хранятся в таблице на восемь записей. Адрес, идентификатор клиента, учётные данные и сессия задаются в MqttConfig. Прежде чем прошивка попадёт на плату, проверьте сервис на хосте: тест объявляет собственную память, и runner ему не нужен.

Тест запускает боевое приложение без изменений на хосте. Embedded TestApp запускает сервис для устройства, а compio TestApp запускает сервис на compio; оба подключают брокер внутри процесса, поэтому сервер и runner не нужны.
cargo add --dev ruststream-rust-mqtt --features testing Тестам нужна фича testing рядом с фичей рантайма сервиса: embassy для устройства, compio для хоста.

Тест объявляет память брокера как static, как это делает плата, и запускает приложение с брокером, созданным через MqttBroker::new над ней. Он публикует в брокер сообщение так, как это сделал бы другой клиент сервера, и проверяет, что получил обработчик и как завершилась доставка. Макросы Вручную examples/device/device_testing.rs #[test] fn a_job_is_answered() { static MEMORY: ConstStaticCell<MqttState> = ConstStaticCell::new(MqttState::new()); block_on(async { let tb = TestApp::start(app(board(MEMORY.take()))) .await .expect("the app starts"); let jobs = tb.broker::<MqttBroker>(); jobs.message(&Sent(b"mix")) .to("jobs/run") .publish() .await .expect("the harness publishes"); jobs.subscriber("jobs/run") .assert_called_once() .with_raw(b"mix") .settled(HandlerOutcome::ack()); jobs.published::<()>("jobs/done") .assert_called_once() .with_raw(b"done"); tb.shutdown().await.expect("the app stops"); }); } examples/manual/device_testing.rs #[test] fn a_job_is_answered() { static MEMORY: ConstStaticCell<MqttState> = ConstStaticCell::new(MqttState::new()); block_on(async { let tb = TestApp::start(app(board(MEMORY.take()))) .await .expect("the app starts"); let jobs = tb.broker::<MqttBroker>(); jobs.message(&Sent(b"mix")) .to("jobs/run") .publish() .await .expect("the harness publishes"); jobs.subscriber("jobs/run") .assert_called_once() .with_raw(b"mix") .settled(HandlerOutcome::ack()); jobs.published::<()>("jobs/done") .assert_called_once() .with_raw(b"done"); tb.shutdown().await.expect("the app stops"); }); }

У теста собственные часы. Копия retry_after возвращается, когда advance переводит часы за её задержку. Макросы Вручную examples/device/device_testing.rs #[test] fn a_job_is_asked_for_again_when_its_delay_has_passed() { static MEMORY: ConstStaticCell<MqttState> = ConstStaticCell::new(MqttState::new()); block_on(async { let tb = TestApp::start(retrying_app(board(MEMORY.take()))) .await .expect("the app starts"); let jobs = tb.broker::<MqttBroker>(); jobs.message(&Sent(b"mix")) .to("jobs/later") .publish() .await .expect("the harness publishes"); tb.advance(Duration::from_secs(4)) .await .expect("the clock moves"); jobs.subscriber("jobs/later").assert_called_once(); tb.advance(Duration::from_secs(1)) .await .expect("the clock moves"); let calls = jobs.subscriber("jobs/later").assert_called(2); assert_eq!(calls.outcomes().last(), Some(&Outcome::Ack)); tb.shutdown().await.expect("the app stops"); }); } examples/manual/device_testing.rs #[test] fn a_job_is_asked_for_again_when_its_delay_has_passed() { static MEMORY: ConstStaticCell<MqttState> = ConstStaticCell::new(MqttState::new()); block_on(async { let tb = TestApp::start(retrying_app(board(MEMORY.take()))) .await .expect("the app starts"); let jobs = tb.broker::<MqttBroker>(); jobs.message(&Sent(b"mix")) .to("jobs/later") .publish() .await .expect("the harness publishes"); tb.advance(Duration::from_secs(4)) .await .expect("the clock moves"); jobs.subscriber("jobs/later").assert_called_once(); tb.advance(Duration::from_secs(1)) .await .expect("the clock moves"); let calls = jobs.subscriber("jobs/later").assert_called(2); assert_eq!(calls.outcomes().last(), Some(&Outcome::Ack)); tb.shutdown().await.expect("the app stops"); }); }

Сервис на compio это вариант с кучей, и его тесту собственная память не нужна. Макросы Вручную examples/mqtt_testing_compio.rs #[test] fn a_job_is_answered_on_compio() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> { Runtime::new()?.block_on(async { let tb = TestApp::start(app()).await?; let jobs = tb.broker::<MqttBroker>(); jobs.message(&Job { id: 7 }) .to("jobs/run") .publish() .await?; jobs.subscriber("jobs/run") .assert_called_once() .with(&Job { id: 7 }) .settled(HandlerOutcome::ack()); jobs.published::<Done>("jobs/done") .assert_called_once() .with(&Done { id: 7 }); tb.shutdown().await?; Ok(()) }) } examples/manual/mqtt_testing_compio.rs #[test] fn a_job_is_answered_on_compio() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> { Runtime::new()?.block_on(async { let tb = TestApp::start(app()).await?; let jobs = tb.broker::<MqttBroker>(); jobs.message(&Job { id: 7 }) .to("jobs/run") .publish() .await?; jobs.subscriber("jobs/run") .assert_called_once() .with(&Job { id: 7 }) .settled(HandlerOutcome::ack()); jobs.published::<Done>("jobs/done") .assert_called_once() .with(&Done { id: 7 }); tb.shutdown().await?; Ok(()) }) } Внутрипроцессный транспорт оставляет серверу постоянную сессию и рукопожатия QoS 1 и 2; их проверяют на живом стенде.
